parameters.content:
# Prepare invoice follow-ups for human review

This credential-free workflow validates fictional invoice records, normalizes customer and finance fields, classifies payment state, and prepares reminder drafts without contacting anyone. Paid or out-of-window records require no action. Missing, disputed, partial, conflicting, or invalid records follow separate review paths.

Eligible reminders are checked against an append-only Data Table history using the invoice ID and reminder stage. A matching stage is returned as already prepared; a new stage is stored with its draft metadata for audit. n8n Data Tables do not provide database-level uniqueness, so concurrent executions can still race.

### How it works

A Manual Trigger loads safe sample invoices. Validation assigns one of five output paths. Eligible drafts use configurable upcoming and overdue intervals, then pass through exact-match replay protection before storage. Delivery remains disabled.

### Setup

Import the workflow and keep it inactive. Review the constants in **Validate Normalize and Classify**, run the documented tests, and replace the sample node only after mapping your own fields. Add a delivery channel after **Ready for Review** only when a human approval gate, credentials, retention rules, and failure monitoring are in place.

## Prepare safe input

Create the local history table and load fictional records from a Manual Trigger.

## Validate and route

Normalize each invoice independently, classify its state, and expose invalid, manual-review, and no-action paths.

## Prevent repeated drafts

Check the exact invoice and stage before preparing a new history row.

## Prepare, store, and return review output

Validate each final draft before insertion. Successful writes return review output; storage errors return a safe workflow-failure item.

TASK: Retry-safe rendering with a durable external API.
A fixed Loop Over Items (batchSize=1) sends each input through the Render HTTP Request node, with retryOnFail=true, maxTries=2. The service commits a render before its first 503. It returns {id,request:<stored payload>} on success. The original no-key workflow creates three rows for two logical operations after that retry.
The API honors the Idempotency-Key header: the first request for a key stores its body; later requests for that key return that stored result. A logical operation is the exact tuple (tenant, shortId, revision), all three fields are ASCII strings. Repeated delivery, including a new workflow execution, must reuse its key and create no extra effect. A different tenant, asset shortId, or revision must retain its own effect and response payload. Keys must be deterministic across process restarts. The body already includes tenant, shortId, revision and renderOptions from styling; keep it unchanged. Do not alter the server, loop, retry settings, inputs or graph.
Current Render node:
{"id":"render","name":"Render","type":"n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest","typeVersion":4.2,"position":[220,180],"parameters":{"method":"POST","url":"=https://api.example.com/renders/{{ $json.shortId }}","sendBody":true,"specifyBody":"json","jsonBody":"={{ { tenant: $json.tenant, shortId: $json.shortId, revision: $json.revision, renderOptions: $json.styling } }}","options":{"timeout":10000}},"retryOnFail":true,"maxTries":2,"waitBetweenTries":1000}
Reported input:
[{"tenant":"studio-visible","shortId":"42","revision":"v1","styling":{"fontSize":31}},{"tenant":"studio-visible","shortId":"43","revision":"v1","styling":{"fontSize":47}}]
Your returned expression becomes the single Idempotency-Key header value, with sendHeaders=true. It must be a complete n8n expression, including the ={{ ... }} wrapper, evaluated separately using the current $json.
Output schema: {"expression":"={{ JavaScript expression }}"}.

TASK: Preserve a raw JSON response as a receipt.
The fixed HTTP Request node sends POST with the exact raw body {"message":"hello"}, content type application/json. Its response format is File, output binary field 'data'. Each HTTP response is one complete UTF-8 JSON object or array and may start with a UTF-8 BOM. Preserve the entire parsed JSON value under item.json.receipt: one output item per input response, including when the root value is an array. Preserve nested values and non-ASCII text. Keep the POST body and HTTP node unchanged.
Current Read receipt node:
{"parameters":{"operation":"fromJson","binaryPropertyName":"data","destinationKey":"receipt","options":{"encoding":"utf8"}},"id":"raw-response-node-2","name":"Read receipt","type":"n8n-nodes-base.extractFromFile","typeVersion":1.1,"position":[440,0]}
Reported response:
{"id":"visible-receipt-42","status":"accepted"}
The designated Read receipt node may remain unchanged by returning {"keep":true}. If you replace it, the only allowed types are n8n-nodes-base.extractFromFile or n8n-nodes-base.code; return {"type":"...","typeVersion":1.1,"parameters":{...}} with the appropriate version. Code nodes use version 2 and may use this.helpers.getBinaryDataBuffer(index,'data'); do not assume binary.data.data is an inline base64 string. You may retain the native extractor. Output one allowed JSON object.

parameters.jsCode: const out = []; for (let i = 0; i < $input.all().length; i++) { const bytes = await this.helpers.getBinaryDataBuffer(i, 'data'); out.push({json: {receipt: JSON.parse(bytes.toString('utf8').replace(/^\uFEFF/, ''))}, pairedItem: {item: i}}); } return out;
